Kealakekua Bay, Hawaiʻi — February 1779

Huakaʻi Pō
Night Marchers — Mobile Edition

You are Captain James Cook. Ashore with a landing party, you will pitch a camp, learn the three rules of the procession by living them, gather the kiʻi from their shrines, and face what the deserter colony fears. Fiction walks beside history here — Cook's real fate at this bay is history's to tell, and this tale does not overwrite it.

The voyage — chapters

A chapter opens only when the one before it is complete — and a chapter is complete only when every kiʻi of that chapter has been gathered from its shrine. Later chapters are named here honestly: locked until earned, and built in later growth passes.

Render scale is how much of your screen's sharpness the game actually draws. The middle two trade a little sharpness for smoothness on their own when the frame rate dips, and take it back when there is headroom. Graphics quality and controller rumble are set in the fixed panel below this sheet — they apply the moment you tap.

Play holding the phone sideways. Left thumb moves, right thumb looks. A paired PlayStation or Xbox controller works too — prompts follow the pad family. Headphones recommended.

AR Procession is a separate mode: the Huakaʻi Pō crosses the room, yard or street in front of your own camera, and the three rules are performed by your real body. It can be played before or after the shore story.

Tilt sensitivity controls how readily the game turns sideways when you tilt the phone (only used when tilt rotation is on). Low — the default — turns only when the phone is held clearly and steadily sideways, and stays sideways until the phone is clearly upright again. Raise it only if the game feels slow to turn.

Controls

Left thumb — move · Right thumb drag — look · Tap right side of screen — Jump · ✋ Use — crates, fire, barrel, rack · 🚪 ENTER — tent flaps only (its own button) · 🙇 BOW — hold still through a pass · Controller (each button does exactly one thing): Cross/A — Use · Square/X — Jump · L1/LB — Enter · Circle/B — Bow · Triangle/Y — Journal · R1/RB — Ukulele.

🗺 Chart of the known coast

Drawn as you discover it: the landing, the camp, the village, the shrine, the heiau, the caches — a place appears on the chart only once your feet have found it.

Guidance controls the objective tracker, the in-world beacon and the edge marker that pings your current objective. Minimal keeps the tracker and the beacon only; Off hides all of it.

⭐ Stars & sky — the naturalist's notes

February, Makahiki season: Makaliʻi (the Pleiades) rides high — the navigator's cluster. Orion's belt stands in the east. Low over the southern ocean glows Hōkū-kea, the Southern Cross, and bright Hōkūleʻa (Arcturus) will climb later in the night. The Milky Way — ke ala o ka Mahina's bright road — crosses the whole sky. Sailors steered by these; the marchers walk beneath them.

Huakaʻi Pō — AR Procession

They cross your space

The Night Marchers walk through the place you are really standing — seen through your rear camera. The three rules stop being buttons: step out of their path with your own feet, bow with your own body, and keep your eyes down — the phone's motion sensors read all three. The drums are the distance meter: loudness and low-pass are how far away they are. 🎧 Headphones recommended.

Safety — read before the first run

Play in an open, familiar space you know by feel. Never near roads, traffic, water, stairs, or drops. You will be looking down with a procession crossing your view — stay aware of the real ground. Seated mode is a full way to play, not a lesser one: bow by lowering and tilting the phone. The ■ STOP button is on screen the whole run — it ends the mode instantly and turns the camera off.

What Phase A is — and is not

Phase A lays the procession over your live camera along a route you calibrate with two taps. It has no surface anchoring (no SLAM) — the line does not lock onto real geometry; no occlusion — the Marchers render over the camera image and will not pass behind your furniture or trees; and the approach distance is staged by time and audio, not measured in your room. Nothing beyond that is claimed. The procession is respected and avoided — never fought — in AR exactly as on the shore.

Pace of the approach

The mode asks for your camera and motion sensors, each with its own plain screen. Deny the camera and the same pass runs in Window mode — against the game's own night, gyro look, full rules. Deny motion and a labelled touch substitute stands in. If this in-app view blocks the camera, open the game in Safari — progress here is session-based, nothing is lost.
